current.text: He is a projected starter for the Spurs with De'Aaron Fox, Devin Vassell, Tobias Harris and Victor Wembanyama.
The Spurs used him as the primary initiator of their offense.
He is expected to lead the Spurs' three guards in minutes because he is versatile on both ends.
The Spurs stagger Fox, Castle and Dylan Harper so that at least two are always on the floor. They may start all three together.
The guard rotation is crowded. More minutes for Harper and a healthy Fox would limit Castle's assists and his upside. One expert does not expect the Spurs to bench Castle or Fox.
He is projected to have about the same usage as last season.

Late last season he shot 40% from three for two months. Earlier in the season his FG%, FT% and three-point shooting were very poor and he turned the ball over a lot. He made his free throws in the Finals.
It is unclear if his late-season shooting is real. His category value depends on whether his three-point shooting holds.
Experts fade him in category leagues at his Yahoo ADP of about 56. They say he goes too early in 9-cat drafts, including in round 5. One expert puts his auction value at about 3 USD.
For category leagues he is ranked in tier 6 among shooting guards and tier 7 among point guards. One expert calls him about right at his ESPN ADP of 75.

durable.text: He is worth much more in points leagues than in category leagues.
His assists are elite and far above the pool.
Creating and passing come more naturally to him, and more reliably, than shooting.
Turnovers are a real problem. His turnover rate is a league outlier.
His free throw shooting is poor for a guard.
Experts call him a poor shooter in general.
He is a versatile defender. He can guard positions one through three, sometimes fours and even small-ball fives.
Experts say his good defense does not turn into many steals and blocks.
He is much less comfortable scoring when he goes left. Defenses can force him left to slow him down.

note: He went for 1 USD in our auction last year. This year Yahoo values him at 13 USD and ESPN at 3 USD, and the category experts fade him at his Yahoo ADP of about 56, so do not pay near Yahoo's number. His 7.3 projected assists help punt FT% and punt TO builds, but turnovers (z -2.2) and FT% cost those builds little, so his price should stay low. Early in the season, check whether his three-point shooting holds and how many minutes Dylan Harper gets.
